correctness.rationale: Independent derivation: at a fixed block count t the optimizer takes the best coordinates in each block. If the unrestricted top-k set has count T>r, the gain for a step ending at t≤r is the t-th largest first-block weight minus the (k−t+1)-st largest second-block weight; the former is in the unrestricted set and the latter is not, so the gain is positive. Hence the constrained count is min(T,r). Uniform strict Gaussian orders and transitivity within each block then give the mass 1/M below r and p/N_r at r (including T=r). Square and sum these masses for the collision law. For x=h/n and y=k/n, Stirling in a fixed standardized window gives the hypergeometric prefactor (2πn x(1−x)y(1−y))^(−1/2) and log exponential −(t−hk/n)^2/[2n x(1−x)y(1−y)]+O(n^(−1/2)) uniformly there: linear entropy terms cancel. This variance proxy differs from the stated variance by a factor tending to one. Riemann summation and Chebyshev outside a fixed large standardized window give the distribution limit. Rounding is negligible; interior collision mass times M/σ_n vanishes, and the boundary mass tends after scaling to (1−Φ(a))²/φ(a)>0. Thus localization holds and multiplication by F/M→Φ(a) yields the uniform-baseline comparison. L<r<U holds eventually under the proportional hypotheses and ensures two distinct masses in the finite result.
